questions: What incorporated definitions and missing dependency determine whether funds are scheme money received or held by the LC or its AE? Those classifications cannot be resolved from the supplied vocabulary alone.

Does “not ‘scheme money’ received or held in Hong Kong” negate scheme-money status alone or the combined status-and-location condition? This may affect the surrounding exclusion and Schedule 11 discussion, but does not supply a defensible rival to the affirmative Q1 trigger.

assumptions: This predicate concerns the selected applicability condition, not whole-law compliance or licence possession.
Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.
The declared input vocabulary is supplied for this controlled comparison; its adequacy as a legal abstraction remains unverified.
The ra13_context input is assumed to capture the stated actor and course-of-Type-13-activity requirements for the funds under examination.
“Regardless of the role” makes transfer-agent status irrelevant once the other stated conditions hold; it does not remove those conditions.
The Schedule 11 discussion states continuing expectations separately from the selected CMR applicability antecedent.
Q2's timing and unknown-receipt qualifications concern its payment-period question and may inform external classification; they are not additional Boolean exceptions to Q1.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).
Generally, the relevant period starts on the day when the receipt1 by the RA 13 LC in Hong Kong becomes scheme money of any relevant CIS.

readings.distinction: Candidate attachments considered are role independence within the expressly qualified applicability proposition, role independence overriding the Type 13 activity condition, and restriction of applicability to transfer agents because Q1 asks about them. Only the first is defensible: “regardless” removes role as an additional condition while preserving the express money, location and activity qualifications. The question's transfer-agent example cannot narrow the answer's general wording. Schedule 11 expectations and Q2's payment timing do not change that attachment. A single reading is therefore retained.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] True means that the selected Q1 applicability antecedent is satisfied: the stated RA13 context, scheme-money classification and Hong Kong receipt-or-holding condition all hold. Transfer-agent status does not change this result. A false result does not determine Schedule 11 obligations or whole-law compliance.
readings.subject: Selected control: the RA13 Client Money Rules Q1 applicability trigger for scheme money received or held in Hong Kong in the course of RA13. Distinguish the transfer-agent role and the continuing Schedule 11 duties. This Boolean concerns only Q1 applicability, not whole-law compliance. Controlled text-interpretation study: supplied pages may be experimental variants. Do not infer legal authority from the URL alone.

vocabulary_concerns: ra13_context compresses actor identity, associated-entity status, handling and the activity nexus; “handling” does not independently establish the source's receipt-or-holding requirement.
in_hong_kong is defined for scheme money, so its meaning for non-scheme money is unspecified. It cannot reliably distinguish rival scopes of the subsequent negative sentence for all funds.
The vocabulary cannot encode Schedule 11 expectations, their relevant paragraphs, or compliance with them. These remain separate from the Q1 predicate.

The vocabulary cannot represent receipt dates, unknown-receipt evidence, account ownership, REIT-property status or the qualified assessment “unlikely to be considered”. Those matters may inform external classifications but cannot be independently tested here.
